entities.name: Senakhtenre Ahmose
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Senakhtenre Ahmose, also known as Ahmose the Elder, was a pharaoh of the Seventeenth Dynasty of Egypt, reigning briefly during the tumultuous Second Intermediate Period, circa 1560–1558 BCE. His rule was confined to the Theban region of Upper Egypt, a time when much of Lower Egypt was under the control of the Hyksos 15th Dynasty. Senakhtenre's significance lies not in grand conquests or monumental constructions, but in his pivotal role as a progenitor and early catalyst for the eventual expulsion of the Hyksos and the reunification of Egypt, a process completed by his descendants. He represents the nascent phase of Theban resistance, maintaining a fragile yet crucial native Egyptian sovereignty against foreign domination.

During his short reign, Senakhtenre Ahmose maintained the Theban dynasty's independence, albeit in a state of vassalage or uneasy truce with the Hyksos rulers based in Avaris. While specific military campaigns or administrative achievements are not well-documented for his rule, his continued presence on the Theban throne solidified the legitimacy of the native Egyptian line, fostering the cultural and political resilience necessary for future confrontation. He likely focused on internal stability within Upper Egypt, preparing the ground for the more aggressive campaigns of his successors. His sarcophagus, discovered in the Dra' Abu el-Naga' necropolis, suggests a king who, despite the limited scope of his power, was afforded the traditional burial rites of a pharaoh.
